selected.title: Who decides what the truck saw
selected.texas_link: The City of Dallas runs AI cameras on its sanitation brush trucks for code compliance, and a Dallas council committee briefing on them is set for October 19th. The film draws a truck, a curb and four checkpoints as an illustration and names no property.

movement.actor: City of Dallas Code Compliance and Sanitation
movement.action: issued its first code citations from camera flags and set a council committee briefing
movement.object: AI cameras on sanitation brush trucks

selected.why_today: A Dallas council committee briefing on the camera program is scheduled for October 19th, 2026, after the city reported its first citations from camera flags.
selected.consequence: A camera flag can lead to a courtesy notice and then to an in person inspection, and a citation follows only after an officer confirms a violation, per the city and press accounts of its memo.
selected.application_change: Code compliance moves from waiting for complaints to photographing curb lines from a truck and letting software flag conditions for staff review.
selected.counter_image: The citation counts are press reports of a memo that was not retrieved, and the program has no completed evaluation. The film doesn't know the outcome of the briefing.
selected.earned_take: The camera only flags. The city says a person and an officer decide, and what the program achieves hasn't been evaluated.

agency.next_step: A Dallas City Council committee hears a briefing on the camera program on October 19th, 2026.
agency.who_can_act: Dallas City Council members and the city manager can change or fund the program, and residents can contact Code Compliance about a notice.

filmability.viewer_question: When a camera on a city truck flags a property, who decides it is a violation?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated Dallas brush truck rolls past a curb pile at street speed and its side camera takes one photo. Disclosed as Illustration.
filmability.mechanism: Input: a still photo of the curb line from the public street. Transformation: software flags listed conditions, an analyst reviews, city workers choose no action, a courtesy notice or a case. Result: a code officer inspects in person before any citation. Limit: the outcome counts come from press reports of a memo that was not retrieved.
filmability.human_consequence: A property owner in Dallas who receives a courtesy notice gets a chance to fix the condition before enforcement. The press reports that 39 of 57 citations fell in three southern council districts. No resident is named and no outcome for any person is claimed.
filmability.source_limit: The September 8th memo with the citation counts was not retrieved, so every count is press reported. Press counts of notices and scanned properties conflict and are not stated. The city's own deck and November memo are dated December 2025 and November 2025. The October 19th briefing has no retrieved agenda or outcome.
three_key_images: A truck camera takes one photo of a curb pile from the street, drawn as an illustration
A photo moves through four checkpoints in order, flag, analyst, notice choice, officer, drawn as a disclosed diagram
A tally of fifty seven citations with thirty nine marked in three southern districts, labelled as press reported, beside a card that says no evaluation has been completed

asset_leads.relevant_image: City deck slides 5 to 7 show a camera on a truck, a staff portal and vendor sample photos.
asset_leads.what_it_proves: The camera form and the staff portal as the city presents them. Not a Dallas capture and not a named property.
asset_leads.inspection: Text extracted from the downloaded PDF. The photographs were not extracted or reused.
asset_leads.rights_basis: None established for the city's or the vendor's photographs, so no photograph is admitted.

action_support.pictured_action: A brush truck passes a curb pile and its side camera takes one still photo of the curb line.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory illustration of the capture the city describes. It shows no Dallas street, no named property and no real software.
action_support.relationship: The city says the side-facing cameras take photos as the truck drives at 25 to 35 miles per hour from the public right-of-way.

action_support.pictured_action: The photo passes four checkpoints in order, software flag, analyst review, notice choice and in person inspection, and a citation waits behind the last.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of the review chain the city and the Dallas Morning News describe. It shows no real portal, no real analyst and no measured accuracy.
action_support.relationship: The Dallas Morning News describes an AI flag, an analyst review, a city decision among no action, a courtesy notice or a case, and an in person inspection before any citation.

action_support.pictured_action: A tally of 57 citations at 34 properties fills in with 39 marked in three southern districts, tagged press reported, beside a card that says no evaluation has been completed.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of reported counts. It shows no property, no map of real addresses and no outcome for any person.
action_support.relationship: Fox 4 and the Dallas Express report the September 8th memo counts and the Dallas Morning News reports that no comprehensive evaluation has been completed.

visual_stakes.opening_question: When a camera on a city truck flags a property, who decides it is a violation?
